summary_en: Introduces a STED-inspired hyper-beamforming method for photoacoustic array imaging. The method forms excitation-like and depletion-like beam patterns and combines them into a narrow, low-sidelobe hyper-beam, while retaining computational complexity comparable to delay-and-sum reconstruction. Phantom and in-vivo experiments report an 83.3% narrower mainlobe and a 25 dB lower sidelobe level than DAS, making this a directly relevant computational photoacoustic imaging paper.
